description: Declared deploy bundle for the Hermes mini spend-control chain: spend_opencode.py (shared billing-route helpers), opencode_exec.py (executor writer delegate), spend_guard.py (hard daily cap), and spend_meter.py (per-provider meter). These four files previously had no manifest and no governed installer, so mini-release-cut.sh's release receipt claimed "governed script deployment verified" even on releases that changed them without ever deploying the change to ~/.hermes/scripts/ (see the v0.18.2/86e2hap1g inert-fix incident in hermes-cron-executes-from-scripts-dir-not-release). This file IS the bundle the installer copies; nothing outside its 'files' list is written. Canon bytes are the live mini copies (all four were vendored verbatim from already-fixed live files, see README.md).

coexist_required.reason: opencode_exec.py dynamically loads claim_store.py from its own directory (importlib.util.spec_from_file_location, not a package import) to record the per-task outcome at session end; a missing copy degrades that outcome bookkeeping. Installer warns, never installs or removes it.

hermes_report_build._row_cost() imports spend_opencode.served_row_cost to strip subscription-covered (Codex OAuth) phantom spend from legacy writer-served rows (86e2hap1g). Owned by the hermes-self-report bundle, not this one; installer warns, never installs or removes it.

files.role: shared billing-route helpers imported by opencode_exec.py, spend_guard.py, and spend_meter.py; classifies Codex-OAuth/subscription-covered rows as $0 marginal cost so the daily cap and meter don't alarm on phantom spend

executor's code-writing delegate (STEP 4 of clickup-queue-poller/SKILL.md); invokes OpenCode, streams the JSON event log, and reports success/failure to the orchestrator; imports spend_opencode for billing-route classification and dynamically loads claim_store.py for the outcome record

hard $50/day spend cap gating every opencode_exec.py delegation; three-tier policy (clean read / stale-cache alarm / no-cache fail-closed) so a state.db or log read hiccup can never silently masquerade as a $0 day; imports spend_opencode for billing-route resolution

per-provider ($/provider/day) companion to spend_guard.py's global cap; a read failure raises SpendDataUnavailable (nonzero exit) instead of returning [] so the spend-meter cron's failure-delivery path fires; no blocking power, informational only; imports spend_opencode for billing-route resolution
